prompt:
This repository is a small invoice library with about 65 commits on the branch main. Running `node --test` in the project folder shows two failing tests: "tax is rounded half up to the cent" (test/tax.test.mjs) and "dueDate adds days to the issue date" (test/dates.test.mjs). Both used to pass. A different commit broke each of them, and every commit after that one still fails the same test. Other tests may change over the history, so judge each commit by the test named here, not by the number of failures.

Do these three things:
1. For each of the two tests, find the first commit where it fails (`git bisect run` with a test name pattern or checking commits one at a time both work). Write both full 40 character hashes to a file named FIRST_BAD.txt in the project root, exactly two lines: `tax <hash>` for the tax test and `due <hash>` for the due date test, in that order, each line ending with a newline and nothing else in the file.
2. Fix both bugs on the current branch so that all tests pass. Do not edit any file in test/. Features that were added after the broken commits must keep working, including the code that was written on top of the broken functions and depends on how they behave today, so do not revert the history or restore old files wholesale: change only what is wrong in the code as it is today. Check the other callers of anything you change.
3. Put FIRST_BAD.txt and the fixes in one new commit on top of the current HEAD with exactly this commit message: `Fix tax rounding regression`.

Do not rewrite, reorder or delete any existing commit (no reset, rebase or amend of old commits). When you finish, you must be on branch main with a clean working tree, and any `git bisect` session must be ended (`git bisect reset`).
